Times Publishing Group | website = {{URL|www.fraserandneave.com}} | footnotes = }} '''Fraser and Neave, Limited''' ('''F&N''') is a Singaporean [[food and beverage]], [[publishing]] and [[printing]] industries conglomerate. Listed in Singapore, the group's subsidiaries include F&N Foods, F&N Creameries, Warbug Group, Yoke Food Industries and Times Publishing. As of 2023, F&N had total assets of over S$5 billion and employed over 7,200 people in 11 countries. In January 2014, through a distribution in specie and re-listing of '''Frasers Centrepoint Limited''' by way of introduction on the Singapore stock exchange, the group de-merged its properties business.{{Cite web |title=About Us: Fraser & Neave |url=http://www.fraserandneave.com/about-us |access-date=24 August 2015 |publisher=Fraser & Neave}} ==History== ===Founding and early history=== [[File:John_Fraser_cartoon.jpg|thumb|left|Caricature of John Fraser]] The company (Singapore and Straits Aerated Water Company) was formed in 1883 by John Fraser and David Chalmers Neave, who diversified from their printing business (Singapore and Straits Printing Office) to pioneer the aerated water business in Southeast Asia in 1883. In 1898, a new public company was formed and the two businesses were sold to the new company, named Fraser & Neave (F&N), for $290,000 in cash and shares.{{Cite news |date=27 January 1898 |title=Fraser and Neave, Ltd |pages=3 |work=Singapore Free Press |url=http://newspapers.nl.sg/Digitised/Page/singfreepressb18980127.1.3.aspx}} ===Diversification, restructuring, and expansion === In 1931, Fraser & Neave formed a joint venture with Holland's [[Heineken International|Heineken]] to venture into the brewing business. The brewery, Malayan Breweries Limited produced [[Tiger Beer]], and later acquired [[Archipelago Brewery]], which produced Anchor Beer.{{Cite book |last=Frankham |first=Steve |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pR4ZZ6Y3kHcC&pg=PA539 |title=Malaysia and Singapore |date=17 June 2008 |publisher=Footprint Travel Guides |isbn=978-1-906098-11-7 |page=539 |access-date=25 April 2012}} In 1936, F&N acquired the Singapore, Malaya and Brunei franchise rights for [[Coca-Cola]] drinks. Alongside its own range of F&N branded drinks, the company went on to acquire the rights to other [[PepsiCo]], Coca-Cola, and [[Cadbury Schweppes Americas Beverages|Cadbury Schweppes]] brands – such as – [[7-Up]], [[Fanta]], and [[Sunkist (soft drink)|Sunkist]]. In 1990, Malayan Breweries changed its name to [[Asia Pacific Breweries]]. ===Modern history=== [[File:F&N Foods logo.jpg|150px|thumb|right|Logo of F&N Foods since 2007]] In 1999, F&N purchased a 20% stake in Times Publishing before taking majority control of the company in 2000, with the entire acquisition costing around S$570 million.{{Cite news |last=Lee |first=H.S. |date=27 April 2000 |title=What's in Times Publishing that attracts F&N? |work=Business Times}} This put F&N into the printing, publishing, retail bookstore, sales and distribution, education, internet and conference organisation businesses. In 2001, F&N took both Times and Centrepoint Properties private. In 2006, the Singapore government investment company [[Temasek Holdings]] took a 14.9%, S$900 million stake in F&N, becoming F&N's second-largest investor.{{Cite news |last=Yap |first=E. |date=9 December 2006 |title=F&N sells 14.9% stake to Temasek for $900m |work=The Straits Times}} In 2008, F&N reorganised its management structure and appointed chief executives for three of its core businesses: food & beverage; property; and printing and publishing.{{Cite news |last=Goh |first=E |date=2 July 2008 |title=More questions than answers in F&N's management revamp |work=The Straits Times}} On 27 June 2007, F&N Singapore launched a new logo for its food and beverage business in order to reach the Asia-Pacific market. In 2010, Temasek's entire stake was sold to Japan's [[Kirin Company|Kirin Holdings]] for S$1.33 billion.{{Cite news |last=Yap |first=E |date=27 July 2010 |title=Temasek exits F&N with $436m profit fizz |work=The Straits Times}} On 1 September 2011, the three-quarter-century partnership between F&N and Coca-Cola in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei ended. F&N no longer had the franchise rights to manufacture and market Coca-Cola beverages. In July 2012, [[ThaiBev]] acquired a 22% stake in F&N from [[Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation]], raising its stake to 24.1%.{{Cite web |title=Thai Beverage increases stake in F&N |url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/singaporebusinessnews/view/1216929/1/.html |access-date=31 July 2012 |publisher=Channel NewsAsia |archive-date=3 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120803022825/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/singaporebusinessnews/view/1216929/1/.html |url-status=dead }} In August 2012, F&N accepted an offer from Heineken to acquire its stake in [[Asia Pacific Breweries]] for US$4.1 billion.{{Cite web |title=Heineken reaches US$4.1b deal for Asia Pacific Breweries |url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_singapore_business/view/1217735/1/.html |access-date=4 August 2012 |publisher=Channel News Asia |archive-date=6 August 2012 partner TCC Assets, both controlled by [[Thai Chinese]] billionaire [[Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi]], made a move to thwart efforts by Heineken to acquire control of Asia Pacific Breweries, with a S$8.8 billion (US$7.1 billion) cash offer for F&N.{{Cite news |date=13 September 2012 |title=Thai group, Heineken in Tiger beer battle |publisher=CNN |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121118092209/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/singaporebusinessnews/view/1225725/1/.html |url-status=dead }}{{Cite news |date=13 September 2012 |title=Thai Billionaire Bids for F&N in Hurdle for Heineken in Asia |work=Bloomberg |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2012-09-12/thaibev-charoen-offers-s-9-billion-for-fraser-neave.html |access-date=14 September 2012}} On 28 September 2012, F&N shareholders approved the sale of Asia Pacific Breweries to Heineken during the extraordinary general meeting held.{{Cite web |title=Heineken takeover of Tiger Beer maker approved |url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_singapore_business/view/1228483/1/.html |access-date=28 September 2012 |publisher=Channel News Asia |archive-date=1 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001003149/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_singapore_business/view/1228483/1/.html |url-status=dead }} In 2013, Kirin Holdings sold its 15% stake in F&N to TCC (ThaiBev).{{Cite web |title=Sale of Shares in Fraser and Neave, Limited and Recognition of Extraordinary Profit |url=http://www.kirinholdings.co.jp/english/news/2013/0201_01.html |access-date=21 June 2015 |website=Kirin Holdings Singapore }} ===Frasers Centrepoint Limited and Frasers Property (2013–present)=== Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi expanded his ThaiBev drinks and property empire to include about two-thirds of this Singaporean [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]].{{Cite news |last=Head |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Head |date=3 February 2013 |title=Thai whiskey tycoon Charoen takes over Fraser and Neave |work=Asia business |publisher=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-21289363 |url-status=dead |access-date=3 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206015921/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-21289363 |archive-date=2013-02-06 |quote=BBC News, Bangkok. What are the secrets of business success in Thailand?}} This was possible after [[Japan]]'s [[Kirin Brewery Company]] sold its 15% stake for US$1.6 billion to Sirivadhanabhakdi.{{Cite news |date=2013-02-04 |title=Thai tycoons go for it in multi-billion deals |publisher=Investvine.com |url=http://investvine.com/thai-tycoons-go-for-it/ |access-date=2013-03-15 |archive-date=2013-02-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130212084623/http://investvine.com/thai-tycoons-go-for-it/ |url-status=dead }} In January 2014, through a distribution in specie and re-listing of '''Frasers Centrepoint Limited''' by way of introduction on the Singapore stock exchange, the group de-merged its properties business. In February 2018, '''Frasers Centrepoint Limited''' was renamed [[Frasers Property]] globally.{{Cite news |last=Nikkei Asian Review |date=1 February 2018 |title=Frasers Centrepoint Renamed Frasers Property |work=Asia business |publisher=Nikkei NewsRise Asia Pte Ltd |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Markets/Nikkei-Markets/Singapore-s-Frasers-Centrepoint-Limited-Renamed-Frasers-Property |access-date=1 February 2018 |archive-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126211002/https://asia.nikkei.com/Markets/Nikkei-Markets/Singapore-s-Frasers-Centrepoint-Limited-Renamed-Frasers-Property |url-status=dead }} ==Products== * [[100Plus]] * Borneo * [[Carnation (brand)|Carnation]] (in Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and Thailand, under license from [[Nestlé]]) * CocoLife * Daisy (a sweetened condensed creamer brand for Philippine distribution) * EST Cola * Farmhouse * Fruit Tree * Ice Mountain * Seasons * [[Magnolia (Fraser and Neave brand)|Magnolia]] * NutriSoy * NutriWell * [[Oishi Group|Oishi]] * Ranger * [[Sarsaparilla (soft drink)#Singapore|Sarsi]] ==References== ===Notes=== {{Reflist}} ===Bibliography=== *{{Cite book |title=Singapore: The Encyclopedia |title-link=Singapore: The Encyclopedia |publisher=Singapore: [[Editions Didier Millet]] |year=2006 |isbn=978-981-4155-63-2 |editor-last=Tommy Koh |editor-link=Tommy Koh |page=205}} ==External links== *[http://www.fraserandneave.com Official site] [[Category:Conglomerate companies of Singapore]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Singapore Exchange]] [[Category:Singaporean brands]] [[Category:Thai brands]] [[Category:Food and drink companies of Singapore]] [[Category:Food and drink companies of Thailand]] [[Category:1883 establishments in Singapore]] [[Category:TCC Group]]
